record.original_question: Does a Riemannian metric on a real projective space with the same volume as the canonical metric have a closed geodesic with length ≤ π?

evidence.quote: Does a Riemannian metric on a real projective space with the same volume as the canonical metric have a closed geodesic with length ≤ π?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n\ge 2$ and let $\mathbb{RP}^n$ denote real projective $n$-space equipped with its canonical Riemannian metric $g_0$ of constant sectional curvature $1$ (the quotient of the round unit sphere $S^n$ by the antipodal map). Under $g_0$, every geodesic is closed of length $\pi$, and the Riemannian volume is $\mathrm{vol}(\mathbb{RP}^n, g_0) = \tfrac{1}{2}\mathrm{vol}(S^n)$.

Question: Does every smooth Riemannian metric $g$ on $\mathbb{RP}^n$ satisfying $\mathrm{vol}(\mathbb{RP}^n, g) = \mathrm{vol}(\mathbb{RP}^n, g_0)$ admit at least one closed geodesic of length at most $\pi$? Equivalently, denoting by $\ell(g)$ the length of the shortest closed geodesic of $(\mathbb{RP}^n, g)$, does $\ell(g)^n \le \pi^n \cdot \mathrm{vol}(\mathbb{RP}^n, g)/\mathrm{vol}(\mathbb{RP}^n, g_0)$ whenever the right-hand side equals $\pi^n$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is widely regarded as open in full generality. A parametric/local version has been established via contact-geometric methods (Álvarez Paiva–Balacheff and follow-ups): along any smooth volume-preserving deformation of the canonical metric that is not formally trivial, the length of the shortest closed geodesic attains a strict local maximum equal to π at the canonical metric, and the analogous result holds for complex and quaternionic projective spaces and the Cayley plane. The global inequality on $\mathbb{RP}^n$ remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Contact geometry and isosystolic inequalities
status_evidence.snippet: Solves a parametric version: along non-trivial volume-preserving deformations of the canonical metric on RP^n (and CP^n, HP^n, OP^2), the shortest closed geodesic length attains a strict local maximum at the canonical metric.
status_evidence.claim: A local/parametric version of the problem is solved; the global statement is the motivating open question.

status_evidence.title: Open problems about geodesics (Burns–Matveev)
status_evidence.snippet: Lists problems concerning shortest closed geodesics and systolic inequalities on projective spaces.
status_evidence.claim: The global isosystolic question on RP^n is recorded among open problems.
